tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

input.prompt:
You are sub-agent 1 of 3 in stage PO-S08 of a JavaScript-to-TypeScript migration of the Audiobookshelf server. Repo: `D:\SEM-2\574\Project\audiobookshelf-po` (Windows; use the Bash tool with POSIX syntax and forward slashes). I am the main agent. Two other sub-agents are converting other controllers in the same working tree right now, so stay strictly inside your own set.

## Your set (9 files; do them in this order, smallest first)
1. server/controllers/StatsController.js (75 lines)
2. server/controllers/CustomMetadataProviderController.js (125)
3. server/controllers/EmailController.js (141)
4. server/controllers/NotificationController.js (153)
5. server/controllers/FileSystemController.js (162)
6. server/controllers/BackupController.js (180)
7. server/controllers/ToolsController.js (180)
8. server/controllers/RSSFeedController.js (204)
9. server/controllers/ApiKeyController.js (207)

## Read first
- `CLAUDE.md` in the repo root, completely. It is the rulebook for this migration. The sections "Rules", "Pitfalls found so far" and "Controllers and Express (PO-S08, from a spike on four controllers)" apply to every line you write. If this brief and CLAUDE.md seem to disagree, CLAUDE.md wins, and you tell me about it in your report.
- `server/controllers/CacheController.ts`: the one controller already converted. It shows the import shape, the TypeScript request types placed above the unchanged JSDoc typedef block, and `export = new CacheController()`.
- `server/routers/ApiRouter.js` (read only): controller methods are bound with `.bind(this)`, so `this` inside a controller method is the ApiRouter instance. Look at its constructor for the properties it has.
- For style, when you need it: any converted `.ts` file in server/models, server/finders, server/managers, server/utils, server/objects.

## Per file
1. Rename: `git mv server/controllers/XController.js server/controllers/XController.ts`. If it fails with an `index.lock` error, wait a few seconds and retry (the other agents use git at the same time).
2. Convert with targeted edits (the Edit tool). Never rewrite the whole file. Existing JSDoc comments stay unchanged.
3. Type-check without emitting:
   `npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json 2>&1 | grep -E "^server/controllers/(ApiKey|Backup|CustomMetadataProvider|Email|FileSystem|Notification|RSSFeed|Stats|Tools)Controller"`
   No lines means your files are clean. The check writes nothing, so it is safe to run while the others work. The unfiltered output contains the other agents' half-finished files; those are not your concern.
4. Behaviour check: `git diff -M HEAD -- server/controllers/XController.js server/controllers/XController.ts`. Apart from imports, type declarations, type annotations, `this: ApiRouter` parameters, the `export =` line and the allowed one-line comments, every line of code must be identical to the original. No new variables, no changed expressions, no reordered statements, no added guards (`?.`, `|| ''`, `String(x)`, an extra `if`), not even to silence the compiler. If the only way to remove an error is to change behaviour, the file "does not fit" (step 5), and the cause usually belongs in the bug log too.
5. If a file cannot pass within the rules of CLAUDE.md, restore it completely: `git mv server/controllers/XController.ts server/controllers/XController.js`, then `git restore server/controllers/XController.js`, then check that `git status --short server/controllers/XController.js server/controllers/XController.ts` prints nothing. # PO-S08: the 22 controllers (a main agent and parallel sub-agents, two waves)

Date: 2026-10-11 (NZDT). Branch Aung-Min-Myat/po-s01 in D:\SEM-2\574\Project\audiobookshelf-po (as in PO-S05 and PO-S07). Stage base: the setup commit "[PO-S08] setup" (the parent of the first commit made by the agent).
Planned settings: Opus 5.5, max effort, auto mode (Shift+Tab in a fresh session, as in PO-S05 to PO-S07), plugins disabled. Cap: 150 minutes after the agent's start.
Who prepared the run: Claude (chat session), on the user's instruction to prepare everything except the Claude Code steps. The user checks /model, /plugin, /permissions and /usage, pastes the prompt and says when it starts and ends.

## Starting state (evidence/test-results/PO-S08/preflight.txt)
- server/controllers: 1 .ts (CacheController) and 22 .js, 9,364 lines in the 22 files. 202 lines in server/routers/ApiRouter.js register controller methods with .bind(this).
- Clean build at the start commit: 0 "error TS", 375 passing, 471 files in dist-server (measured in a Linux clone by Claude, not on the user's machine).
- Compiled baseline for the later comparison: D:\SEM-2\574\Project\po-s08-baseline, 471 files, a Windows build at the setup commit with 375 passing and 0 "error TS" (built in a copy of the repo with identical sources and the same node_modules, not in audiobookshelf-po itself).
- Permission rules: .claude/settings.local.json unchanged since PO-S07 (copy: settings.local.before.json). Mode acceptEdits, 17 allow rules, 15 deny rules plus a PowerShell deny rule from outside the file. Edit(test/**), Edit(server/libs/**), Edit(package.json), Edit(package-lock.json), Edit(tsconfig.server.json), Edit(tsconfig.check.json) are denied. The user's /permissions screen before the run showed the same lists.
- Baseline panel (user, 2026-10-11 03:54): session 2% used, week (all models) 63%, week (Fable) 51%, total cost $0.0000, wall 2m 31s. That session was not used for the run; a fresh one is used and /usage is copied again just before the paste.

## What this run is
- Target: all 22 JavaScript controllers. Express request types, the .bind(this) calls from the JavaScript ApiRouter, and req.query/req.body/req.files are new problems compared with the models (Sequelize) and the leaf files of earlier runs.
- Structure like PO-S05: a main agent, sub-agents in two waves (wave 1: 3 sub-agents, 5,240 lines; wave 2: 2 sub-agents, 4,124 lines), only the main agent builds, tests and commits.
  - Set 1: ApiKey, Backup, CustomMetadataProvider, Email, FileSystem, Notification, RSSFeed, Stats, Tools (1,427 lines).
  - Set 2: Me, User, Session, Share (1,957).
  - Set 3: Search, Series, Author, Collection, Playlist (1,856).
  - Set 4: Library, Misc (2,288).
  - Set 5: LibraryItem, Podcast (1,836).
- The hard files (Library 1,500 lines with 49 req.query uses; LibraryItem 1,251 lines) are in wave 2 on purpose: the main agent has the wave 1 evidence and commits before they start.

## What this run changes compared with PO-S05 (the other multi-agent run)
1. A different job: controllers (Express, this binding, HTTP input) instead of Sequelize models.
2. CLAUDE.md was extended before the run (commit "[PO-S08] setup"): a new section "Controllers and Express"; the stale "Done so far" line and the test count (356 -> 375) were corrected; rule 5 was cleaned (it contained a repeated clause) and gets three controller allowances.
3. Three sub-agents in wave 1 and two in wave 2 (PO-S05: four in wave 1, then a second wave on the models not reached).
4. The time limits are longer: wave 1 stops at 60 minutes, wave 2 at 120, the run ends at 150 (PO-S05: 50, 100, 120). The user wants the run to finish the job, and the controllers are larger than the models.
5. The agent writes a bug log (bugs are listed, not fixed). In PO-S07 the bugs were fixed with tests; here the rule is again "type-only".
6. The checkpoints are taken by Claude from the user's repo every 15 minutes (read-only git commands), not by a script that the user runs.
The changed variables (the job, the guidance, the limits) mean that the results cannot be credited to one of them.

## Operator spike (disclosure; this is not a run)
Before the run, Claude converted four controllers (Stats, Backup, Search, Series) in a separate Linux clone to find out which TypeScript patterns the controllers need. The clone is not part of the repo and nothing from it was committed. All four compiled with 0 errors, the build passed and 375 tests passed; the compiled files differ from the baseline only in the require lines (the express destructure disappears; one destructured require gets an intermediate variable) and in trailing comments (checked with a diff of the four compiled files). Findings that went into CLAUDE.md:
- A class method that is registered with .bind(this) needs an erased first parameter `this: ApiRouter` (the JavaScript ApiRouter type is inferred, so this.backupManager and the like type-check). A middleware method may use this without a @this tag.
- req.query is a union type (string | ParsedQs | ...). The Request generics (Request<Params, ResBody, Body, Query>) avoid a cast at every use.
- A catch variable is unknown, so `(error as Error).message` appears at every catch that reads the message.
- A comparison of a query value with a number (SearchController: query.podcast === 1) is flagged as impossible (TS2367). It is an original bug (a query value is never a number) that the types cannot express.
- A middleware sets properties (req.backup, req.series, req.libraryItemsInSeries); the middleware and the handlers need different request types (optional and required).
- libs/fsExtra has no type for mkdir (it is added in a loop), BookFinder.search takes a weak type that a podcast item does not share a property with, and toOldJSON() results get properties added after the call.
The spike was done by Claude, who knew the earlier runs and the repo, so its duration says nothing about the time an agent will need.

## Decisions taken by Claude for the user (for the report; the user can reverse them)
1. CLAUDE.md allowances for controllers: `(error as Error)` on catch variables (one comment per file), `(x as unknown) === y` for a comparison the types call impossible (listed in the bug log), and one call-site cast into a converted file whose parameter type is too narrow. Reason: without them the agent would have to skip almost every controller, because every catch block would fail. Risk: the cast count rises and a strict reading of rule 5 (PO-S07) would not allow them. They are counted separately in the report.
2. The leaf-first order is waived for controllers (they require Logger, Database, SocketAuthority and other unconverted files).
3. The setting files were not changed, so the Edit(test/**) deny rule stays and the sub-agents cannot edit tests.
4. ApiRouter.js and the root files stay JavaScript. The agent may not edit them.

## Measurements planned
- /usage before and after (usage-start.txt, usage-end.txt) and the end-of-run cost.
- Checkpoints every 15 minutes from the repo (run-log.txt): time, commits, .ts and .js counts in server/controllers, git status summary.
- Prompts answered by the user and the "Recently denied" list, recorded at the end. Session backup (the user runs the log backup function) for the exact prompt time, the sub-agent count, tokens and cost per agent.
- After the run: scope and protected paths (no change outside server/controllers/ and evidence/), banned tokens and escape hatches (!, casts, index signatures) counted by our own scan, every commit built and tested on its own, a compiled-output comparison for each controller against the baseline (the require lines and comments may differ), five clean builds at the end, and an API smoke comparison of the baseline and the final build.

## Predictions (written before the run; the numbers are guesses)
1. 19 to 22 of the 22 controllers are converted (best guess 21). If any is skipped, LibraryController or LibraryItemController is the most likely, then PodcastController.
2. Every commit builds and passes 375 tests on its own (the main agent integrates after each wave).
3. The run takes 80 to 140 minutes (best guess 110); the first wave ends within its 60 minutes.
4. The cost is between $35 and $80 at API prices (PO-S05: $39.57 for 14 models; this job has about twice the number of files and lines). Best guess $55.
5. The cast count is high because of the catch variables: 60 to 200 `(error as Error)` sites. The count of `!` is below 10.
6. The compiled-output comparison finds that at least 18 of the 22 controllers differ from the baseline only in the require lines and comments. One to three controllers show a change in the code (a new variable, an added ?. or a changed order), because the agents tend to "fix" what the types complain about.
7. The bug log lists at least 10 real bugs or doubtful spots in total.
8. The week limit (63% used at the start) is not reached during the run. If it is reached, the run is recorded as interrupted.

## Replies policy
If the agent asks a question or a permission prompt appears, the user answers in a few words and counts it. The user does not give hints about the code.

# PO-S08: the 22 controllers (a main agent and parallel sub-agents, two waves)

Date: 2026-10-11 (NZDT). Branch Aung-Min-Myat/po-s01 in D:\SEM-2\574\Project\audiobookshelf-po (as in PO-S05 and PO-S07). Stage base: the setup commit "[PO-S08] setup" (the parent of the first commit made by the agent).
Planned settings: Opus 5.5, max effort, auto mode (Shift+Tab in a fresh session, as in PO-S05 to PO-S07), plugins disabled. Cap: 150 minutes after the agent's start.
Who prepared the run: Claude (chat session), on the user's instruction to prepare everything except the Claude Code steps. The user checks /model, /plugin, /permissions and /usage, pastes the prompt and says when it starts and ends.

## Starting state (evidence/test-results/PO-S08/preflight.txt)
- server/controllers: 1 .ts (CacheController) and 22 .js, 9,364 lines in the 22 files. 202 lines in server/routers/ApiRouter.js register controller methods with .bind(this).
- Clean build at the start commit: 0 "error TS", 375 passing, 471 files in dist-server (measured in a Linux clone by Claude, not on the user's machine).
- Compiled baseline for the later comparison: D:\SEM-2\574\Project\po-s08-baseline, 471 files, a Windows build at the setup commit with 375 passing and 0 "error TS" (built in a copy of the repo with identical sources and the same node_modules, not in audiobookshelf-po itself).
- Permission rules: .claude/settings.local.json unchanged since PO-S07 (copy: settings.local.before.json). Mode acceptEdits, 17 allow rules, 15 deny rules plus a PowerShell deny rule from outside the file. Edit(test/**), Edit(server/libs/**), Edit(package.json), Edit(package-lock.json), Edit(tsconfig.server.json), Edit(tsconfig.check.json) are denied. The user's /permissions screen before the run showed the same lists.
- Baseline panel (user, 2026-10-11 03:54): session 2% used, week (all models) 63%, week (Fable) 51%, total cost $0.0000, wall 2m 31s. That session was not used for the run; a fresh one is used and /usage is copied again just before the paste.

## What this run is
- Target: all 22 JavaScript controllers. Express request types, the .bind(this) calls from the JavaScript ApiRouter, and req.query/req.body/req.files are new problems compared with the models (Sequelize) and the leaf files of earlier runs.
- Structure like PO-S05: a main agent, sub-agents in two waves (wave 1: 3 sub-agents, 5,240 lines; wave 2: 2 sub-agents, 4,124 lines), only the main agent builds, tests and commits.
  - Set 1: ApiKey, Backup, CustomMetadataProvider, Email, FileSystem, Notification, RSSFeed, Stats, Tools (1,427 lines).
  - Set 2: Me, User, Session, Share (1,957).
  - Set 3: Search, Series, Author, Collection, Playlist (1,856).
  - Set 4: Library, Misc (2,288).
  - Set 5: LibraryItem, Podcast (1,836).
- The hard files (Library 1,500 lines with 49 req.query uses; LibraryItem 1,251 lines) are in wave 2 on purpose: the main agent has the wave 1 evidence and commits before they start.

## What this run changes compared with PO-S05 (the other multi-agent run)
1. A different job: controllers (Express, this binding, HTTP input) instead of Sequelize models.
2. CLAUDE.md was extended before the run (commit "[PO-S08] setup"): a new section "Controllers and Express"; the stale "Done so far" line and the test count (356 -> 375) were corrected; rule 5 was cleaned (it contained a repeated clause) and gets three controller allowances.
3. Three sub-agents in wave 1 and two in wave 2 (PO-S05: four in wave 1, then a second wave on the models not reached).
4. The time limits are longer: wave 1 stops at 60 minutes, wave 2 at 120, the run ends at 150 (PO-S05: 50, 100, 120). The user wants the run to finish the job, and the controllers are larger than the models.
5. The agent writes a bug log (bugs are listed, not fixed). In PO-S07 the bugs were fixed with tests; here the rule is again "type-only".
6. The checkpoints are taken by Claude from the user's repo every 15 minutes (read-only git commands), not by a script that the user runs.
The changed variables (the job, the guidance, the limits) mean that the results cannot be credited to one of them.

## Operator spike (disclosure; this is not a run)
Before the run, Claude converted four controllers (Stats, Backup, Search, Series) in a separate Linux clone to find out which TypeScript patterns the controllers need. The clone is not part of the repo and nothing from it was committed. All four compiled with 0 errors, the build passed and 375 tests passed; the compiled files differ from the baseline only in the require lines (the express destructure disappears; one destructured require gets an intermediate variable) and in trailing comments (checked with a diff of the four compiled files). Findings that went into CLAUDE.md:
- A class method that is registered with .bind(this) needs an erased first parameter `this: ApiRouter` (the JavaScript ApiRouter type is inferred, so this.backupManager and the like type-check). A middleware method may use this without a @this tag.
- req.query is a union type (string | ParsedQs | ...). The Request generics (Request<Params, ResBody, Body, Query>) avoid a cast at every use.
- A catch variable is unknown, so `(error as Error).message` appears at every catch that reads the message.
- A comparison of a query value with a number (SearchController: query.podcast === 1) is flagged as impossible (TS2367). It is an original bug (a query value is never a number) that the types cannot express.
- A middleware sets properties (req.backup, req.series, req.libraryItemsInSeries); the middleware and the handlers need different request types (optional and required).
- libs/fsExtra has no type for mkdir (it is added in a loop), BookFinder.search takes a weak type that a podcast item does not share a property with, and toOldJSON() results get properties added after the call.
The spike was done by Claude, who knew the earlier runs and the repo, so its duration says nothing about the time an agent will need.

## Decisions taken by Claude for the user (for the report; the user can reverse them)
1. CLAUDE.md allowances for controllers: `(error as Error)` on catch variables (one comment per file), `(x as unknown) === y` for a comparison the types call impossible (listed in the bug log), and one call-site cast into a converted file whose parameter type is too narrow. Reason: without them the agent would have to skip almost every controller, because every catch block would fail. Risk: the cast count rises and a strict reading of rule 5 (PO-S07) would not allow them. They are counted separately in the report.
2. The leaf-first order is waived for controllers (they require Logger, Database, SocketAuthority and other unconverted files).
3. The setting files were not changed, so the Edit(test/**) deny rule stays and the sub-agents cannot edit tests.
4. ApiRouter.js and the root files stay JavaScript. The agent may not edit them.

## Measurements planned
- /usage before and after (usage-start.txt, usage-end.txt) and the end-of-run cost.
- Checkpoints every 15 minutes from the repo (run-log.txt): time, commits, .ts and .js counts in server/controllers, git status summary.
- Prompts answered by the user and the "Recently denied" list, recorded at the end. Session backup (the user runs the log backup function) for the exact prompt time, the sub-agent count, tokens and cost per agent.
- After the run: scope and protected paths (no change outside server/controllers/ and evidence/), banned tokens and escape hatches (!, casts, index signatures) counted by our own scan, every commit built and tested on its own, a compiled-output comparison for each controller against the baseline (the require lines and comments may differ), five clean builds at the end, and an API smoke comparison of the baseline and the final build.

## Predictions (written before the run; the numbers are guesses)
1. 19 to 22 of the 22 controllers are converted (best guess 21). If any is skipped, LibraryController or LibraryItemController is the most likely, then PodcastController.
2. Every commit builds and passes 375 tests on its own (the main agent integrates after each wave).
3. The run takes 80 to 140 minutes (best guess 110); the first wave ends within its 60 minutes.
4. The cost is between $35 and $80 at API prices (PO-S05: $39.57 for 14 models; this job has about twice the number of files and lines). Best guess $55.
5. The cast count is high because of the catch variables: 60 to 200 `(error as Error)` sites. The count of `!` is below 10.
6. The compiled-output comparison finds that at least 18 of the 22 controllers differ from the baseline only in the require lines and comments. One to three controllers show a change in the code (a new variable, an added ?. or a changed order), because the agents tend to "fix" what the types complain about.
7. The bug log lists at least 10 real bugs or doubtful spots in total.
8. The week limit (63% used at the start) is not reached during the run. If it is reached, the run is recorded as interrupted.

## Replies policy
If the agent asks a question or a permission prompt appears, the user answers in a few words and counts it. The user does not give hints about the code.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build and test one commit on its own, outside the repo.
# Usage: verify-commit.sh <commit-ish> <label>
# Exports the commit's tree with git archive into the scratchpad, links the repo's node_modules with a
# junction (nothing is installed), then runs the same two commands as "npm test":
#   tsc -p tsconfig.server.json   and   mocha dist-server/test
# The repo's working tree and index are not touched.
set -u
REPO="D:/SEM-2/574/Project/audiobookshelf-po"
S="C:/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--SEM-2-574-Project-audiobookshelf-po/6e0ca4b8-675c-4688-bcf2-09dd5cccaab0/scratchpad"
COMMIT="$1"
LABEL="$2"
DEST="$S/verify-$LABEL"

if [ -e "$DEST" ]; then
  echo "destination exists: $DEST" >&2
  exit 2
fi
mkdir -p "$DEST"
git -C "$REPO" archive "$COMMIT" | tar -x -C "$DEST"
# junction, removed again at the end with rmdir (which removes only the link)
cmd //c "mklink /J $(cygpath -w "$DEST/node_modules") $(cygpath -w "$REPO/node_modules")" > /dev/null

cd "$DEST" || exit 2
echo "== $LABEL ($(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --short "$COMMIT")) build"
node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.server.json > build.txt 2>&1
BUILD_RC=$?
echo "build exit code: $BUILD_RC, error TS lines: $(grep -c 'error TS' build.txt)"
head -20 build.txt
if [ $BUILD_RC -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "== $LABEL test"
  node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js dist-server/test > test.txt 2>&1
  echo "mocha exit code: $?"
  grep -E "^\s+[0-9]+ (passing|failing|pending)" test.txt
fi
cmd //c "rmdir $(cygpath -w "$DEST/node_modules")"
[ -e "$DEST/node_modules" ] && echo "WARNING: junction still present" >&2
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build and test "base commit + some converted controllers from the working tree", outside the repo.
# Usage: verify-overlay.sh <base-commit> <label> Name1 Name2 ...      (names without "Controller")
# For each name the working tree's XController.ts is copied in and the exported XController.js is removed,
# which is exactly the tree a commit of those controllers on top of <base-commit> would have.
# Then the same two commands as "npm test" run there. The repo's working tree and index are not touched.
set -u
REPO="D:/SEM-2/574/Project/audiobookshelf-po"
S="C:/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--SEM-2-574-Project-audiobookshelf-po/6e0ca4b8-675c-4688-bcf2-09dd5cccaab0/scratchpad"
BASE="$1"
LABEL="$2"
shift 2
DEST="$S/overlay-$LABEL"

if [ -e "$DEST" ]; then
  echo "destination exists: $DEST" >&2
  exit 2
fi
mkdir -p "$DEST"
git -C "$REPO" archive "$BASE" | tar -x -C "$DEST"
for NAME in "$@"; do
  SRC="$REPO/server/controllers/${NAME}Controller.ts"
  if [ ! -f "$SRC" ]; then
    echo "missing $SRC" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  cp "$SRC" "$DEST/server/controllers/${NAME}Controller.ts"
  rm -f "$DEST/server/controllers/${NAME}Controller.js"
done
# the working tree's server/types (only the main agent edits it) so that added declarations are included
cp "$REPO"/server/types/*.d.ts "$DEST/server/types/"

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. - Sequelize associations are the recurring wall. `declare libraryFolders?: …` and absent `getX()` mixins in the converted models are correct-but-incomplete types, and they can only be completed in `server/models/`, which this run may not touch.

content.text:
## PO-S08 report

**14 of the 22 controllers are converted, 8 were restored because they do not fit the rules, and none was left unreached.** Final state at `d89acaf7`: `npm run build:server` 0 errors, `npm test` **375 passing**, working tree clean. The run took 89 minutes (04:33:33 to 06:02; limit 150).

### Per set

| Set | Converted | Skipped (restored) | Not reached |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Backup, CustomMetadataProvider, Email, FileSystem, Notification, RSSFeed, Stats, Tools | ApiKey | none |
| 2 | Me, Share | Session, User | none |
| 3 | Series, Search, Author | Collection, Playlist | none |
| 4 | Misc | Library | none |
| 5 | none | LibraryItem, Podcast | none |

Why each was skipped (the decisive compiler errors):

- **ApiKey**: the sub-agent converted it with 0 errors, and I restored it. It needs two casts for the `getUser()` mixin that the converted `ApiKey.ts` does not declare (TS2339); no allowance covers a missing member of a converted file.
- **Session**: Sequelize's typings reject `where: null` (TS2769, original line 69), and `user.username` is read on a user that can be null (TS18047, line 316).
- **User**: 33 errors. Among them are `Database.getPlaybackSessions(where = null)` inferred as null-only (TS2345), a nested `include` given as an object (TS2353), unguarded `.join` on optional permission arrays (TS18048) and a number assigned to the Date field `lastSeen` (TS2322).
- **Collection**: 32 errors. A `.find()` result is read unguarded (TS18048), `getOldJsonExpanded()` is called 8 times without its required `user` (TS2554), and the `getCollectionBooks` mixin is undeclared (TS2339, 5 places).
- **Playlist**: 33 errors. Four `.find()` lookups are read unguarded (TS18048, 9 places), a required argument is missing (TS2554), and `changed()?.length` is read on `false | string[]` (TS2339).
- **Library**: 122 errors. The `getLibraryFolders()` mixin is undeclared (TS2551, once on a local instance), a nested `include` is rejected (TS2353, 3 places), and fields of converted models are optional or unknown (TS18048, TS18046).
- **LibraryItem**: 126 errors. Three groups of `.find()` results are read unguarded (TS18048, 26 places), and a wrong type is assigned to `Book.ebookFile` (TS2322).
- **Podcast**: one blocker left. The result of `getFileTimestampsWithIno()` can really be `false` and is read unguarded (TS2339, 4 places). Only a cast on an accurate type would compile, so I did not allow it.

### What was added

| Item | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Non-null assertions (`!`) | 3 | Notification 111, Author 107, Misc 100 |
| Index signatures | 10 | Misc 4, Author 3, Series 2, Search 1 |
| Casts, Allowance 1 | 1 | Search 122 |
| Casts, Allowance 2 | 5 | Search |
| Casts, Allowance 3 | 5 | Search 102, Author 143, Me 470 (two), Misc 745 |
| Casts, other | 15 | all on untyped JavaScript modules, see below |
| `this: ApiRouter` parameters | 21 | Backup 7, Tools 4, Me 4, Misc 4, Email 2 |

The 15 other casts, by cause:
- **7** narrow the `media` union or a typedef of `LibraryItem.js` (Author 77, 162, 222, 271; Email 131; Me 521; Share 102).
- **4** are on an argument passed to a JavaScript callee whose JSDoc parameter is too narrow (Author 448, Share 133, Misc 238 and 260).
- **2** are for inherited Sequelize statics of the still-JavaScript `LibraryItem` model (FileSystem 160, Share 270).
- **1** is for `libs/fsExtra` (Backup 129).
- **1** is for a wrong JSDoc return type in `AbMergeManager.js` (Tools 85).

Also added: one `this: PublicRouter` (Share), a file-local `declare function isNaN(value: unknown)` in Me and Share, and four annotated destructured imports. Banned tokens: 0.

### Decisions I took (you can reverse them)

1. **Rule 5 read strictly**, as the PO-S07 notes describe it. A cast is accepted only where the type it corrects comes from an untyped JavaScript module, or under Allowances 1 to 3. That is why ApiKey was restored although it compiled.
2. **`!` allowed on `library.libraryFolders`** (Misc 100). It is an association field that `findByIdWithFolders()` always sets before the read. My wave-2 brief had excluded "an optional array", which was stricter than CLAUDE.md; I corrected it at 05:41 and sub-agent 4 then converted Misc. This cost that agent about ten minutes.
3. **Four casts on arguments to JavaScript callees accepted**, although rule 5 literally says "returns".
4. **I edited `server/types/untypedModules.d.ts`** (3 lines: `uuid.validate` and `uuid.version` for Share). Your prompt allows this; the PO-S08 scope line in CLAUDE.md says no file outside `server/controllers/`.
5. **Two small edits of my own in converted files**: `(await x) as T` became `await x as T` in Author (4 lines, removes parentheses from the compiled file), and `req.files` became a required property in Misc (commit `d89acaf7`).

Sub-agents 2 and 3 each used `sed -i` once, against the brief, on a file they later restored completely; nothing of it remains.

### Bug log (all sub-agents)

63 entries. Line numbers are those of the original `.js` files. All were found by reading the code; none was executed or confirmed by a test, and none was fixed.

- **ApiKey**
  - 179–189 (possible): `delete` has no root check, unlike `create` and `update`.
  - 139: the log message in `update` says "cannot be created".
- **Author**
  - 100: `update()` accepts `null` as name and stores it.
  - 138: merging two authors pushes the existing author twice when a book already has both.
  - 315: the log prints `imagePath` where the name is meant.
- **Backup**
  - 71: `req.files.file` is read without a guard on `req.files`.
- **Collection**
  - 384: `removeBatch` answers 500 where `addBatch` answers 400.
  - 152: `description` is stored without the type check that `create()` has.
  - 48, 170, 320, 382: `books` is never checked with `Array.isArray`.
  - 199, 215, 257, 302, 305, 364, 367, 420 (possible): `getOldJsonExpanded()` is called without the user, so the responses are not filtered by the user's restrictions.
  - 2: `Sequelize` is required but unused.
- **CustomMetadataProvider**
  - 45–54 (possible): the raw url is stored, not the validated one.
- **Email**
  - 135 (possible): a non-admin gets 404 where other controllers answer 403.
- **FileSystem**
  - 30–34: `?path=a&path=b` gives an array and `Path.isAbsolute` throws.
- **Library**
  - 915: the log interpolates `req.user` and prints `[object Object]`.
  - 380–389: `update()` does not validate folder entries.
  - 1163, 1211, 628, 630: `libraryFilters.decode()` can return null and is used unchecked.
  - 133–137 (lower confidence): client folder objects are passed unfiltered into `create`.
- **LibraryItem**
  - 72, 115, 563: a query string is compared with the number 1 using `==`.
  - 669–679: `batchUpdate` reads `mediaPayload` fields without checking that the entry has one.
  - 231, 283: `updated` in the response can be the URL string instead of a boolean.
  - 500–501, 670–672, 1036–1038: `.find()` results are used without a guard.
  - 742–743: `batchGet` answers 403 for an invalid payload.
  - 1186–1194: the stored ebook file does not match `EBookFileObject`.
- **Me**
  - 298–304: an object with a `length` property reaches `for...of` and throws.
  - 486: a negative `limit` drops items from the end.
  - 160–161, 203–204: `page` and `itemsPerPage` are not validated (same entry as User 437–438).
  - 644–645: the JSDoc says plain `Request` (documentation only).
- **Misc**
  - 92–93: two uploaded files with the same field name give an array, and `Path.join` then throws.
  - 667–721: `updateAuthSettings` also loops over the read-only `authOpenIDSamplePermissions` key.
- **Notification**
  - 106–107: `updateNotification` ignores the `:id` in the URL and uses `req.body.id`.
  - 79–84: `createNotification` answers 200 when the payload is rejected, and a body without `urls` throws.
- **Playlist**
  - 431: `addBatch` throws when `episodeId` is not an episode of the item.
  - 44–45: `create()` lacks the array checks that `addBatch` has.
  - 113–123, 555–565: work continues in the `try` after `commit()`, so a later throw calls `rollback()` on a finished transaction.
- **Podcast**
  - 100, 112, 120–122: the stat result can be `false`, so the item is created with `ino` undefined and zero timestamps.
  - 155–171: the pushed cover file has `fileType` and no `isSupplementary`.
  - 295: `?limit=` (empty) gives 0 instead of the default 3.
  - 351: `findEpisode` answers 500 for a missing `title`.
  - 392: copied log message.
  - 378: `isAutoDownload` is omitted (a JSDoc inaccuracy).
- **RSSFeed**
  - 157: passes `req.body` where the sibling handlers pass `reqBody` (inconsistency only).
- **Search**
  - 116: `query.podcast === 1` can never be true.
  - 44: the JSDoc documents a parameter that does not exist.
  - 94: `findBooks` loads any item by id without an access check.
- **Series**
  - 83: `update()` does not check for a duplicate name, and `save()` has no try/catch.
- **Session**
  - 316: `user.username` is read on a deleted user's session.
  - 36–39: an invalid `user` query returns every user's sessions.
- **Share**
  - 69–72, 103, 122: an invalid session cookie is cleared, then reused and set again.
  - 396–398, 46: `removeMediaItemShare()` is not awaited, and the row is deleted twice.
  - 266–272: after a failed zip stream, `res.status(500)` is called on a response whose headers are sent.
  - 327, 360: the slug is tested trimmed but stored untrimmed.
  - 38: `"1e3"` passes `isNaN` and becomes 1.
- **Stats**
  - 53: the log prints `NaN`, not the raw year.
- **Tools**
  - 70: `cancelEncode()` is not awaited.
  - 31, 36, 41, 46, 161: log messages name the wrong controller.
  - 113: `libraryItemIds` is not checked to be an array.
- **User**
  - 347, 424: `user_updated` is emitted to the acting admin, not the changed user.
  - 130, 255: a null from `hashPassword()` is stored unchecked.
  - 294, 298: `.join` on optional permission arrays.
  - 325: a number is assigned to `lastSeen`.
  - 320–321: `isActive` is compared as boolean but stored raw.
  - 41–42: `.sort` is called on a possible `false`.

### Did CLAUDE.md work as written?

**Yes for the 14 converted controllers.** The import shape, the request types and generics, the erased `this: ApiRouter`, the three allowances, the widening annotations and the `declare const global` pattern all applied as described. The "Debug Failure" crash did not occur.

**It did not cover what blocked the other 8:**

1. **Unguarded lookups and nullable values**: `.find()` results, a user that can be null, a helper that can return `false`. No allowance exists, and a guard is a behaviour change. This blocked Collection, Playlist, LibraryItem, Session and Podcast.
2. **Sequelize associations on converted models**: undeclared mixins (`getUser`, `getCollectionBooks`, `getLibraryFolders`), association fields declared optional, and associations missing on index-signature models. None can be fixed inside `server/controllers/`. This blocked ApiKey, Collection and Library.
3. **Calls that omit an argument a converted method now requires** (TS2554); a cast cannot supply an argument.
4. **Sequelize's own typings narrower than the runtime**: `where: null`, a nested `include` as an object, `changed()?.length`.
5. **`LibraryItem.js` still being JavaScript**: every inherited static needs a boundary cast per call site. This worked, but the section does not mention it.
6. **JavaScript callees with a too-narrow parameter**:
   - Rule 5 says "returns", so an argument cast is not literally covered.
   - "Annotate the destructured import once" is rejected by the compiler in that case (TS2322).
   - A `= null` default is inferred as null-only.

Smaller gaps:
- Handlers bound by PublicRouter need `this: PublicRouter`.
- "Generics once per controller" does not fit controllers with several bodies.
- "Query values are strings" is false in LibraryController, whose middleware rewrites `limit` and `page` as numbers.
- Allowance 2 names `.message` only.
- `isNaN` on a string needs a file-local declaration.
- The grep in the check command hides the lines under a multi-line error.

### Final build and test

| Commit | Content | Build | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c4c94aa3` | set 1 (8 controllers) | 0 errors | 375 passing |
| `bcb90db8` | set 2 (Me, Share, uuid declarations) | 0 errors | 375 passing |

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. ALWAYS call search_design_system first to find existing components, variables, and styles to reuse — never generate components from scratch if a design system match exists.
3. For web app pages, use both tools in parallel: generate_figma_design to capture a pixel-perfect screenshot, and use_figma to build the screen from imported design system components. Refine use_figma output against the screenshot, then delete the screenshot reference.
4. For non-web targets (iOS, Android, generic UI), use use_figma with search_design_system.
5. For updating or syncing a Figma page that has already been captured, use use_figma — even if the source code has changed.

FROM-SCRATCH DESIGN WORKFLOW (no source design or code):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if… [truncated]
